name: Universal Ajax Filter
author: Prostil Mangasule

pratapvashi123.display_name: Pratap Patil - Walstar Technologies Pvt Ltd

sections.description:
Universal Ajax Filter lets you build front-end filter bars that refresh results instantly via AJAX — without writing a single AJAX handler. Create as many filter sets as you need from a simple admin screen, then drop each one into a page using a shortcode or the plugin’s own Elementor widget.

Each filter set can combine multiple fields — Search, Dropdown/Select, Checkbox, Radio, and Buttons (pill style) — bound to any taxonomy and its terms, and can drive one of four result actions:

  • Query Posts – filter standard WordPress posts
  • Query Products – filter WooCommerce-style product post types
  • Filter CPT – filter any custom post type on your site
  • Load Elementor Template – render matching items through an Elementor Pro Loop Item template

Key Features

  • Visual filter builder — add, reorder, and remove filter fields from the admin screen; no code editing needed.
  • Multiple filter types — Search, Dropdown/Select, Checkbox, and Radio, each bindable to any taxonomy and specific terms.
  • Four result actions — Query Posts, Query Products, Filter CPT, or Load an Elementor Template, so one tool covers blogs, shops, and custom content types.
  • Shortcode support — every saved filter gets its own shortcode, e.g. [psaf_smart_ajax_filter id="12"], ready to paste into any page, post, or widget area.
  • Native Elementor widget — search for “Universal Ajax Filter” in the Elementor panel and configure a filter directly inside the page editor, with no shortcode or saved filter needed.
  • Elementor normal grid support — when using the standard Elementor editor, filtered results can be displayed using a regular Elementor grid without requiring Elementor Pro.
  • Elementor Pro Loop Grid support — filter results can be rendered using Elementor Pro Loop Grid and Loop Item templates, allowing you to use your custom Loop Item designs. Elementor Pro is required for Loop Grid/Loop Item functionality.
  • Layout & Style options — choose filter position (left, top, right), card style (Classic, List, Overlay, Minimal), columns per device, gap, image height, colors, shadows, corner radius and pagination style from the dashboard, with one-click presets.
  • Gutenberg block — add the “Universal Ajax Filter” block and adjust the layout from the block sidebar; no shortcode needed.
  • Shortcode attributes — override the layout per page, e.g. [psaf_smart_ajax_filter id="12" position="top" columns="4" card_style="overlay"].
  • Custom results target — results load by default into a .psaf-results container, or you can point the filter at your own CSS selector to filter an existing grid on the page.
  • Configurable pagination and sorting — set results per page, order-by field, and sort direction per filter.
  • Custom loading and empty-state text — set your own “Loading…” and “No results found.” messages per filter.
  • Multiple filters per site — build unlimited independent filter sets, each with its own configuration, shortcode, and widget instance.
  • Lightweight front end — vanilla AJAX requests with dedicated frontend CSS/JS assets, only loaded where needed.

How It Works

  1. Go to Universal Ajax Filter → Add New in the WordPress admin menu.
  2. Choose a post type, result action (Query Posts, Query Products, Filter CPT, or Load Elementor Template), results-per-page, and sort order.
  3. Add one or more filter fields (Search, Dropdown/Select, Checkbox, Radio) and bind each to a taxonomy and, optionally, specific terms.
  4. Save the filter — you’ll get a ready-to-use shortcode, e.g. [psaf_smart_ajax_filter id="12"].
  5. Paste the shortcode into any page or post, or open Elementor and drag in the “Universal Ajax Filter” widget to configure the same filter directly in the builder.
  6. Visitors filter results instantly on the front end — no page reload.

Requirements

  • WordPress 5.8 or higher.
  • PHP 7.4 or higher.
  • Elementor (free) is only required if you want to use the native Elementor widget — the shortcode works with any theme or page builder.
  • Elementor Pro is only required if you choose the “Load Elementor Template” result action to render results through a Loop Item template.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the prostil-smart-ajax-filter folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin zip through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Universal Ajax Filter → Add New to create your first filter.
  4. Copy the generated shortcode into a page/post, or add the “Universal Ajax Filter” widget from the Elementor panel.
sections.faq:
Do I need Elementor to use this plugin?

No. The shortcode [psaf_smart_ajax_filter id="X"] works on any theme or page builder. The Elementor widget is an optional, additional way to add and configure a filter directly inside the Elementor editor.

Can I filter WooCommerce products?

Yes. Choose the “Query Products” result action and set the post type accordingly when creating a filter.

Can I filter a custom post type?

Yes. Choose “Filter CPT” as the result action and select your custom post type from the Post Type dropdown.

Can filters target an existing results grid on my page instead of generating their own?

Yes. By default results load into a .psaf-results container, but you can set a custom CSS selector as the results target in the filter settings to hook into your own existing grid.

Does this work with Elementor Loop Item templates?

Yes, if Elementor Pro is active. Set the result action to “Load Elementor Template” and select the Loop Item template you want filtered results rendered through.

Can I create more than one filter?

Yes. Create as many independent filter sets as you need from Universal Ajax Filter → Add New — each has its own configuration, shortcode, and can also be added as a separate Elementor widget instance.

How do I change the layout when I use the shortcode in the block editor?

Open Universal Ajax Filter → Edit and use the Layout & Style card (position, card style, columns, colors and more). To change it for just one page, either use the Universal Ajax Filter block and its sidebar settings, or add attributes to the shortcode, for example [psaf_smart_ajax_filter id="12" position="top" columns="4" card_style="overlay" accent="#2563eb"]. Supported attributes: position (left, top, right), columns, columns_tablet, columns_mobile, card_style (classic, horizontal, overlay, minimal), gap, image_height, card_radius, card_shadow (none, soft, strong), card_hover, show_image, show_excerpt, excerpt_lines, accent, card_bg, card_border, title_color, text_color, panel_bg, panel_radius, input_radius, pagination_style, class.

How do I choose what a WooCommerce product card shows?

Set the filter’s post type to Product, then open Layout & Style → Product card in the filter editor. You can also set it per page, for example [psaf_smart_ajax_filter id="12" show_cart="no" show_category="yes" button_text="Buy now"], or with the Universal Ajax Filter block’s Product card panel. Attributes: show_badge, show_rating, show_price, show_cart, show_category, show_stock, show_sku, show_description (yes or no), button_style (filled, outline), button_width (full, auto), button_text, badge_style (pill, square), badge_position (left, right).
sections.changelog:
1.2.0 (in progress)

  • New: Buttons (pill style) filter type — a taxonomy filter shown as clickable buttons, with single or multiple selection and an optional, renameable “All” button.
  • New: “Filter buttons” styling in Layout & Style, the shortcode (fbtn_* attributes), the Gutenberg block and a new “Filter Buttons” section in the Elementor Style tab: shape, size, text weight, alignment, wrap or scroll layout, spacing and normal / hover / active colors.
  • New: Price slider filter type — a two-handle range slider with min/max number inputs, available in the filter editor and the Elementor widget. Works with WooCommerce prices or any custom price field.
  • New: WooCommerce product card for product filters — sale badge, star rating, price and add to cart button.
  • New: “Product card” options in Layout & Style, the shortcode and the Gutenberg block: show or hide badge, rating, price, add to cart, category, short description, stock status and SKU, plus button style, button width, button text, badge shape and badge position.
  • Shortcode and block overrides are now kept when results reload through AJAX.

1.1.0

  • New: “Layout & Style” card in the filter editor — filter position, card styles, columns (desktop/tablet/mobile), gap, image height, colors, shadow, radius, pagination style and presets.
  • New: Gutenberg block with layout and style controls in the editor sidebar.
  • New: layout and style attributes for the [psaf_smart_ajax_filter] shortcode.
  • Fix: pagination now sits under the results when filters are on the left.
  • Existing filters keep their current look until a style option is changed.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: visual filter builder, Search/Dropdown/Select/Checkbox/Radio filter types, AJAX results, shortcode support for Posts, Products, and custom post types.
